grand_strategy.reading:
Kenya plays the strategy of a middle power without a hegemon's resources: it
has no oil, an exhausted treasury and a restless street, and what it can sell
is the room itself. It hosts the talks nobody else can host (South Sudan's
Tumaini track, the DRC process, even the founding charter of the Sudanese army's enemy), supplies
police and soldiers to missions that other states design (Haiti, AUSSOM),
shelters the UN's Nairobi offices, and takes money from everyone who wants a
voice in East Africa - China's yuan loans, Gulf fuel credit, Washington's
health compact, London's training ground, Brussels' preferences. Luttwak's
reading is that the position is rented, not owned: the broker is indispensable
only while the great powers need a neutral address, and each act that proves
indispensability - the RSF charter, Madobe's Jubaland, the Haiti command - is
the one that draws a retaliation (Sudan's import ban), a quarrel (Mogadishu)
or a bill (Haitian crowds, Gen Z at home). Domestically the clock is the 2027
election: the Odinga pact that carried Ruto's broad-based government died
with Raila on 15 October 2025, and every foreign choice is made with the
street and the debt service (interest about 45% of ordinary revenue) in view.
Signals that are not rows. First, a 'two pillars' formula attributed to Ruto
was not found in any source read; what the sources do record is
'a bridge between East and West' (Beijing, April 2025), which is a hedge
rather than a choice. Second, the US embassy in Nairobi lacked a confirmed
ambassador for a long stretch of 2026 although the December 2025 health
compact was signed in Washington: the American attention is real but thin.
Third, Kenya recognised Morocco's sovereignty over Western Sahara in April
2026 and Kosovo in March 2025: recognition looks like a currency Nairobi spends
where partners pay, an unsentimental turn from its old non-aligned posture
(our reading, not a sourced motive). The
open question is the Odinga succession: if ODM fractures, the foreign
portfolio loses its domestic anchor before the vote.
